content.text:
Read it, plus the set it points at (vc-x1 `main` `a4309084fdfe`) diffed against ours.

## What is being asked

vc-x1's cycle `docs: the family agent-files proposal` produced **one set** (`AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, `agent-data/*`) meant to be adoptable as-is by any project, customized through `custom.md`. Base is zc-ring-x1's set as landed 2026-08-26, with vc-x1's seven listed changes on top. They want it reviewed **as rules, not instances**. On agreement wink copies it into `vc-x1-template/work`, fixes two template fossils (`jj-tips.md`, the pre-0.75.0 `.vc-config.toml`), and every member re-syncs. Acceptance check: the three-way comparison going empty, `custom.md` and `TODO.md` excepted.

Done when: we accept, or counter in their mailbox naming what we differ on.

## The shape of the change for us

Size: our agent-files are 2872 lines, theirs 2126. Ours has `cycle-protocol.md` at 931 lines alone.

**Structure.** `cycle-protocol.md` and `cycle-checklists.md` are gone. The protocol is stated once, in `AGENTS.md`, in ~185 lines. Every rule becomes one sentence and a link, and every *why* moves to `agent-data/rationale.md` under a heading that mirrors the rule's 1:1. The other agent-data files carry no inline why at all, only `[why]` links. Three new files: `rationale.md`, `cycle-model.md` and `commit-model.md` (worked specimens, not skeletons), and `messaging.md`.

**Records.** One `TODO.md`, with `## Closed` as the history: the last cycle's record, and after that the landmark commit's tree holds it. `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` **freeze** - never appended, never backfilled, still linked and still read as history. That is the largest behavioral change for us: chores-07 is our live record file, and there are 130 references into the chores files from outside `notes/chores/`.

**Todo format.** Entries become `###` headings, cited by link, priority by file order, **no numbers**. `TODO.md` gains `## Continuation notes`, `## Waiting`, `## Ideas`, `## Bugs`. Our `vc-x1 fix-todo` renumbering stops applying.

**`custom-family.md` dissolves.** Its three jobs split: messaging into the new universal `agent-data/messaging.md` driven by a config `[family]` table, the validation commands into a config `[validate]` table run by `vc-x1 validate`, and member/template paths into `[family]`. The dogfood log has no successor - the diff is the proposal set and the cycle record is the history. Worth knowing: `rationale.md` names our `custom-family.md` by name as the *measured* failure justifying the new rule "a rule adopted ahead lives in the agent-file, never a holding section". This proposal is in part about us.

**Config carrier.** `.vc-config.toml` becomes `.vc-config.md` (markdown with toml blocks, `[repos]` / `[family]` / `[validate]`). Ours is doubly stale - still the pre-0.80.0 `bot` spelling, and `vc-x1 config --validate` exits 1 on it today. Installed vc-x1 is 0.80.5, so the tooling is already ahead of us.

## Rule changes with teeth

- **Versioning**: ours is "scope decides, minor for architecture". Theirs is "patch by default, minor by the user's call, major by the project's promise", and the agent never infers minor from content or size. I think this is the right direction - it removes a judgment call the agent was making badly - but it is a real reversal of a rule we wrote.
- **Cycle shape is fixed at the first push**, and a ladder lands as a trapezoid or kept separate, **never squashed** (every rung's `ochid:` is a change id and a squash discards all but one).
- **Per-rung flow gains two explicit review stops**: a work review ("please review" as its own message, no title or body) before any description is written, then a description review before the push.
- **At rest**: the agent says everything worth saying *before* the final publishing command, then replies with the single word "Published" and stops.
- **Close-out gains step 4** (record the agent-files line count in `notes/agent-files-size.md`, smaller being a "quasi-goal") **and step 7 Restart**, writing `## Continuation notes` for the next agent.
- **Dev artifact name**: the built artifact carries `<name>-dev` while a cycle runs, restored at Land.
- **Typeable punctuation** is demoted from its own rule to a Prose style item.
- **Rules become an unordered bullet index**, no numbers - so every "hard rule N" citation in our records becomes uncitable by number. The names stay, and a review cites by name.
- Terminology: "bot repo" is retired for **"agent-repo"**, always hyphenated.

## Points I would consider countering on

1. **There is no `## File map`.** Their `AGENTS.md` dropped it, but `rationale.md` still carries a mirrored `## File map` heading reading `_None recorded._`. By that file's own rule that is a finding, not a gap. Practically, an agent now learns which agent-data files exist only by tripping over an inline link, and `rationale.md`, `cycle-model.md`, `commit-model.md` and `messaging.md` are never enumerated anywhere.
2. **`rationale.md`'s per-file sections are incomplete.** It says "one `##` per agent-file" but has none for `messaging.md`, `cycle-model.md`, `commit-model.md`, or itself.
3. **Where design findings go is unspecified.** The cycle-record rule says a finding that must outlive the cycle "goes into a `notes/` file", with chores frozen and no named home. For us that means inventing a file per finding. Worth asking what they intend.
4. **The dogfood log's 9 in-flight entries need dispositions** before `custom-family.md` dissolves - most are accepted per their 2026-08-21 record, but not all, and dissolving the file without walking them loses the open ones.
5. **Two small corrections** (their rule sends corrections straight into the payload): `AGENTS.md` line 209 has an unbalanced paren, "distinct within its cycle [Commit description details][cdd])."; and `[cbt]` and `[cdd]` are two labels resolving to the identical anchor.
6. `notes/agent-files-size.md` with "smaller being the quasi-goal" institutionalizes a pressure against clarity at every close-out. Arguable either way, worth a sentence.

My read: the substance is good and mostly better than what we carry - the one-place-per-rule structure, the why/rule split, and the single record home all fix things our own dogfood log has been complaining about. Points 1 and 2 are structural enough to be worth naming in a counter rather than swallowing, and 3 and 4 are questions we need answered to adopt at all. Points 5 and 6 are small.

The adoption itself is not a re-sync-by-copy for us: `TODO.md` reformats, `custom-family.md` dissolves three ways, the config carrier converts, and 130 chores references have to survive the freeze. That is its own cycle, likely a multi-step one.

The plain version: vc-x1 wants us to adopt their rewritten instruction set, which is shorter and better organized but changes how we keep records, retires `custom-family.md`, and moves our validation commands into the config file. Nothing in it looks wrong to me. I have six things I would raise, two of them real gaps. Adopting is a cycle's worth of work, not a copy.

Want me to draft the counter, accept outright, or open a cycle to do the adoption?

# Todo and cycle record

This file contains near term tasks with a short description and reference links to more details.
Its shape is [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next: working copy state, the step in flight, an
open question. Ephemeral, never a record. Written before a restart or when a session is about to
lose context, read first at acquaint, acted on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader.

_None._

## In Progress

A cycle's record has one home at a time, and while the cycle runs this is it. The block's
shape is the specimen in [cycle-model.md](agent-data/cycle-model.md), and the rules are in
[The In Progress block](agent-data/notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

### feat: segmented seam-word SPSC v1
## Closed

The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). Earlier cycles are in the landmark commit's copy
of this section, and the cycles before the rule in the frozen [notes/chores/](notes/chores) and
[notes/done.md](notes/done.md).

## Waiting

Important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on, in a form that can be
checked, and the rank it takes in `## Todo` once unblocked. Every opening checks each condition
and promotes what is met ([Opening](AGENTS.md#opening)).

_None._

## Todo

Entries are in priority order, the first highest, and reprioritizing is moving an entry. Each is a
`###` heading, so a citation is a link to its anchor. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form).
Deeper detail goes in a `notes/` design file (link via `[N]` ref).

### Descriptor queue endpoints

Paired DescSender (loan + send) / DescReceiver (recv) [[11]]:
- own ring endpoint + registry access
- the demo's ~20-line send path becomes ~3 lines
- `resolve`'s unsafe is audited once inside the crate (recv safe by construction)
- guard handed back on Full
- design against both ring flavors (SPSC + MPSC)
- the sender is also where each sender's private overflow pending list will live.

### Overflow FIFO

On ring Full, append the message to a sender-private pending list instead of failing
[details](notes/ring-buffer-design.md#overflow-fifo-future):
- intrusive: the same embedded next-link the free-stack uses, so zero allocation
- naturally bounded by pool capacity
- composes per-sender with MPSC, see [Overflow
  readiness](notes/ring-buffer-design.md#overflow-readiness).

### Batch alloc/free demo

Alongside the one-message alloc_free_1t loops, a variant that allocs X messages (5, 10, ...) then
frees them all, pool vs global allocator. We think the pool's rate stays constant (pop/push is O(1)
regardless of live count, LIFO keeps the working set hot) while Box::new/drop slows as the batch
outgrows malloc's thread-cache fast path, and the demo should show it.

### Endpoint claims word

CAS-claimed producer/consumer roles in the ring header so a second attach/split claimant gets an
error instead of silently violating SPSC, at the cost of a layout_version bump (or spends `_pad0`)
[details](notes/ring-buffer-design.md#resolved-questions).

### Typed endpoints

`Producer<T>` / `Consumer<T>` validating `T`'s geometry once at split instead of asserting on every
reserve_slot_with [details](notes/ring-buffer-design.md#api).

## Ideas

Unranked, not yet solid enough for `## Todo`. Triaged at an opening: promoted to `## Todo` or
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md), folded into a picked-up cycle, or dropped.

- Perf benches live in [iiac-perf](https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf) (sibling repo
  `../iiac-perf`), not here. Its calibrated harness compares zc-ring against mpsc et al. directly
  (`zcring-1t`/`zcring-2t` mirroring `mpsc_1t`/`mpsc_2t`). An in-repo bench only if per-commit
  regression tracking proves necessary.

- Fan-in helper: consumer-side composition polling N SPSC rings under a pluggable service policy
## Bugs

_See [bugs.md](notes/bugs.md)._

Alongside the one-message alloc_free_1t loops, a variant that allocs X messages (5, 10, ...) then
frees them all, pool vs global allocator. We think the pool's rate stays constant (pop/push is O(1)
regardless of live count, LIFO keeps the working set hot) while Box::new/drop slows as the batch
outgrows malloc's thread-cache fast path, and the demo should show it.

### Endpoint claims word

CAS-claimed producer/consumer roles in the ring header so a second attach/split claimant gets an
error instead of silently violating SPSC, at the cost of a layout_version bump (or spends `_pad0`)
[details](notes/ring-buffer-design.md#resolved-questions).

### Typed endpoints

`Producer<T>` / `Consumer<T>` validating `T`'s geometry once at split instead of asserting on every
reserve_slot_with [details](notes/ring-buffer-design.md#api).

[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md), folded into a picked-up cycle, or dropped.

# Known bugs

This file uses [Prose form](../agent-data/prose.md#prose-form). It lists known defects we're aware
of but haven't scheduled a fix for. Each entry describes what goes wrong, when, and the cost of the
failure. Entries are numbered (`1.` `2.` ...), an index rather than a rank. Run
`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run notes/bugs.md` to renumber after an insert, delete, or reorder.

## Bugs

1. Pool free-stack CAS is not cfg-gated: `src/pool.rs` calls `compare_exchange` unconditionally, so
   the whole crate fails to build on load/store-only targets (thumbv6m), contradicting the design's
   "the atomic floor rises only for pool users". The MPSC module gates on
   `target_has_atomic = "32"`, and pool (and registry, which uses Pool) should gate the same way.
   Found while adding the gate for MPSC (0.11.0-1).

# Bugs

This file uses [Prose form](../AGENTS.md#prose-form). It
lists known defects we're aware of but haven't scheduled a fix for.
Each entry describes what goes wrong, when, and the cost of
the failure. Entries are numbered (`1.` `2.` …) the same way
as `## Todo` in `../TODO.md`; run
`vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run notes/bugs.md` to renumber after
insert / delete / reorder.

## Bugs

1. 2t benches accept a 1-CPU pin pool and livelock through spin
   handoffs. `core_for` wraps the pin pool (`src/harness.rs`),
   so e.g. `iiac-perf zcr-mpsc-2t --pin 8` pins both the main
   thread and the spinning echo worker to core 8. Neither side
   yields, so every handoff waits for an involuntary preemption
   (milliseconds instead of ~200 ns) — the 5×1,000-step cost
   estimate alone takes minutes and the run appears hung.
   Observed on 3900x 2026-07-26; `--pin 8,9` behaves normally.
   Cost: an apparent hang the user must ^C, with no hint that
   the pinning was the cause. The bug requires pinning — an
   unpinned run lets the scheduler separate the threads and
   behaves normally. Fix direction:
   - Track `core_for` requests in `RunCfg` (max `thread_idx`
     asked for): thread placement only goes through `core_for`
     when pinning is active, so refusing a pool with fewer
     unique CPUs than requested placements covers every path
     to this bug — no per-bench thread-count declaration
     needed.
   - Independently, put a wall-clock deadline on the open-loop
     5×1,000-step estimate phase so *any* pathologically slow
     bench aborts with a diagnostic instead of hanging.
   - Update 2026-08-02 (0.24.0): the deadline half is fixed structurally: the estimate phase is
     gone, and every warmup pass is deadlined by the warm cap (`--warm-cap`, default 1.5 s), so
     the hang shrinks to a bounded wait ending in an "uncertified" report. The pool-size guard
     half remains open (the run still livelocks through the measurement itself).

# References

# vc-x1 config file

Configure the work-repo of a dual repo system. The other repo, we call the agent-repo, is
also a markdown configuration file typically named .vc-config.md.

The code blocks in these config files are in toml format and these blocks are logically
concatenated in the order written here and those become the information used for configuring
the system. The [vc-config.md](vc-config.md) contains the documentation for the
various toml tables used for configuration and it is also used during compilation to define
the valid contents of this file.

The file [vc-config-test.md](vc-config-test.md) is a simple version of this file.
(I think we might rename the file vc-config-test.md to vc-config-model.md and it should
also contain every table and key/value pair showing typical or default values, my thoughts)

The two repos
- work [[1]]
- bot [[2]]
```toml
[repos]
work = "."
agent = ".claude"
```

The agent-file family this repo belongs to: its member name and the sibling repos it answers to
- member [[3]]
- template [[4]]
- messages [[5]]
```toml
[family]
member = "zc-ring-x1"
template = "../vc-x1-template"
messages = "../vc-x1-messages"
```

The validation commands, each element one invocation, run in order by `vc-x1 validate`
- full [[6]]
- fast [[7]]
```toml
[validate]
full = [
  "cargo fmt",
  "cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings",
  "cargo test",
  "cargo install --path . --locked",
]
fast = ["cargo test --bins"]
```

content.text:
Looked at `../zc-ring-x1` directly. It is running the proposed set live, and its copy is byte-identical to vc-x1's except **one line**, which is itself a live counter-proposal (below). That is much stronger evidence than the proposal document alone.

## The four you named, as they actually look

**Chores and done are frozen, and nothing migrates.** `notes/chores/chores-01.md`, `-02.md` are untouched, and `notes/done.md` gained a four-line header:

> Frozen history: the `## Done` entries of cycles that ran before the cycle record became `TODO.md > ## In Progress` alone. Nothing is added here ([Frozen history](...)).

That is the whole migration. Every `[[N]]` ref into the old files still resolves. This answers the worry I raised last turn about our 130 chores references: none of them move, none break. The cost is only that the two record systems sit side by side, with the boundary being a date.

**Close-out simplified from 9 steps to 7**, and the three that went are exactly the record-duplication ones. Ours today: move the block into `chores-NN.md`, write a separate `## Done` entry, then backfill as-built ladder refs after landing. All three are replaced by one line - move the block whole to `## Closed`. The opening also loses its `## Done` sweep. Two steps are new: record the agent-files line count, and Restart (write `## Continuation notes`, then the user restarts the agent). Net effect is that a rung is written once and never transcribed, which is the rationale file's stated reason: "detail written twice drifts".

**`TODO.md` is now the whole record file**, 263 lines in zc-ring-x1, holding `## Continuation notes`, `## In Progress` (the live cycle-record, ~110 lines of it), `## Closed`, `## Waiting`, `## Todo`, `## Ideas`, `## Bugs` (a pointer), `# References`. Each section carries a short paragraph stating its own rule, so the file teaches its own shape. Todo entries are `###` headings with no numbers, cited by anchor link, priority by file order. Their `## Ideas` is a real working section - unranked, triaged at each opening into Todo, backlog, a cycle, or dropped.

**bugs.md keeps its numbers**, and the tweak is the justification: "Entries are numbered (`1.` `2.` ...), **an index rather than a rank**. Run `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run notes/bugs.md` to renumber." So the drop-the-numbers rule is Todo-only, and `fix-todo` keeps a job. Two things our copy needs anyway: its prose-form link points at `../AGENTS.md#prose-form`, which is stale (theirs points at `../agent-data/prose.md#prose-form`), and our one bug entry carries an em dash and a `×`.

Also worth having seen: `notes/agent-files-size.md` is a real table with a guard clause I was wrong to worry about - "The count is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it." Drop my point 6 from last turn.

## What zc-ring-x1's use has already produced

They adopted on 2026-08-28 as `docs: adopt the family agent-files set` (2126 lines), then immediately ran a second cycle, `docs: keep the ladder markers in the closed block` (2129), which **reverses** vc-x1's close-out step "drop the `(current)` / `(done)` markers". Their argument, in their rationale: the finished block is the ladder as it was worked, a closed block is one whose every rung reads `(done)`, so a rung reading otherwise is a finding - and dropping them is one more transform of the record, of exactly the kind the new cycle-record rule retired.

They are right, and it is their own rule being applied against vc-x1's text. If we accept, we should accept zc-ring-x1's version of that line, not vc-x1's.

## One finding that is load-bearing

`agent-data/messaging.md` **is linked from nothing** - not `AGENTS.md`, not `custom.md`, not any other agent-data file, in either member. I grepped both. Because the set also dropped `## File map`, an agent following the set as written never learns the file exists, which makes its first rule - "At acquaint, check the record file" - unreachable dead text.

That is not hypothetical for us. This session found the vc-x1 proposal only because our `custom-family.md > ## Messaging` says to look, and this proposal dissolves that file. Adopting as written would mean the next session stops checking the mailbox.

The fix is one line in `AGENTS.md`, either restoring a `## File map` or adding a messaging bullet to `## Working practices`. Their own rationale rule ("a heading with nothing under it but `_None recorded._` is a finding") already flags the orphaned `## File map` heading sitting in `rationale.md` with no section to mirror.

## Where I land

Given zc-ring-x1 is running it well, I would **accept, with a short counter** naming three things rather than disputing the design:

1. `messaging.md` must be reachable - one line in `AGENTS.md`.
2. Take zc-ring-x1's markers-stay line over vc-x1's drop-markers step.
3. Two corrections straight into the payload: `AGENTS.md` line 209 has an unbalanced paren, and `rationale.md`'s `## File map` heading mirrors a section that no longer exists.

Everything else I flagged last turn is either answered by seeing it in use (design findings go to `notes/` design files, as `ring-buffer-design.md` does) or is small enough to carry.

Our own adoption is still a cycle's work and is mostly config and structure, not judgment: `.vc-config.toml` -> `.vc-config.md` with `[repos] agent`, `[family]`, `[validate]` (ours fails `vc-x1 config --validate` today), `custom-family.md` dissolving three ways, `TODO.md` reshaping, and the dogfood log's 9 in-flight entries needing dispositions before that file goes.

The plain version: zc-ring-x1 has been living on this set and it works, the chores freeze costs nothing because nothing moves, and close-out really does get shorter by dropping three copy-the-record steps. One genuine bug: the messaging file is orphaned, so adopting as-is would silently stop us checking the mailbox. Accept with a three-point counter.

Want me to draft that counter record for their mailbox, or open the adoption cycle first?

# vc-x1-messages v0.1.0

Notifications for the vc-x1 family. Message bodies live in the sender's own repo, this repo holds
only pointers to them, one record per message.

The version above is the record format's, and changes to it are additive. A field is added, never
renamed or repurposed, so a reader written against an older version still reads today's records.
A major bump would mean that stopped being true and there has not been one.

To send a message create a file with the message and a markdown section header somewhere in your
repo. Then add a record to the file named for the destination you find here, directly below that
file's own header, so the newest record is first. Whether a push sits between those two steps is
[the choice of mode](#two-modes-fast-and-durable) below. A record is a `##` heading and a list of
fields and each field is generally "owned" by the creator, although fixing errors is
permissible. Every field is optional and records routinely carry only two or three, though a
writer aims for at least one of `local` or `remote`, since a record with neither points at
nothing.

## 2026-08-13T19:31:21.123Z iiac-perf

- local: [../iiac-perf/messages/test-msg.md#message1](../iiac-perf/messages/test-msg.md#message1)
- remote: https://github.com/winksaville/iiac-perf/blob/55554b452957/messages/test-msg.md#message1

The heading is `<utc-timestamp> <sender>`. It is also the record's anchor, so a reply or a
record elsewhere can link at this exact entry without anyone inventing an id.

Then a dash list of `- field: <value>`, where every reference may carry an optional markdown
section slug.

- `local:` the message's local file reference.
- `remote:` the message's remote file reference.
- `read:` added by the recipient, a UTC timestamp of when they read it. A record without it is
  unread. Receipt is not completion: a record stays open until it carries an outcome, so a
  member's open traffic is the records in their file with no `outcome-*` field, and `read` is
  what tells the sender their message arrived.
- `outcome-local:` / `outcome-remote:` optional, added by the recipient, pointing at what came of
  the message, the reply or the record of what was decided. They are what let one record hold
  both halves of an exchange, and their arrival is what closes a record.

A handled record, this one sent the other way, as it would sit in `iiac-perf.md`. Two things are
worth noticing. The body is vc-x1's specimen under `notes/messages/` where iiac-perf's sits
under `messages/`, because a body lives wherever its sender chooses. And the `remote:` was
written only after the body's commit pushed, the ordering rule from
[Two modes](#two-modes-fast-and-durable) obeyed in this very example, since a permalink cannot
precede the commit it names. The exchange is staged but every reference is live:

## 2026-08-13T20:41:33.512Z vc-x1

- local: [[1]]
- remote: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/blob/437a1e6b93d2/notes/messages/test-msg.md#message1
- read: 2026-08-13T22:04:07.000Z

**Fields may be added later without breaking what is already written**, which is why a record is
a list of named fields rather than a positional line. A reader ignores fields it does not know,
and a record missing an optional field is complete as it stands. Prose may sit beside the fields
in a record, only the field lines are read. A record carries no version of its own, since its
commit dates it against this file's history.

**A malformed record is not an error, only less useful**, and a reader takes what is there rather
than rejecting it. A heading that lost its sender is even recoverable, since whoever wrote a
record committed it. The one part that must be present is the `##` heading itself, because it is
what separates one record from the next. Field lines with no heading above them are read as part
of the record before, so an interrupted write damages its neighbour rather than itself.

## Two modes, fast and durable

The message file lives in your repo either way. What differs is whether the record carries a
permalink, and that decides both the order of the steps and how long the record stays good for.

- **Fast, local only.** Write the message file, add the record with `local` alone, done. No push
  and no waiting, and the reader resolves it from their sibling clone.
- **Durable.** Write the message file, commit and push it, then add the record with the `remote`
  that push made resolvable.

**The order matters only in the durable mode, and it is the step people miss.** A permalink names
a commit, so it cannot be written before that commit exists and is pushed. Write the record first
and you have a URL that 404s until the file catches up with it.

**Write a record once, when you have what goes in it.** Writing it early with an empty `remote`
costs two writes to this repo for one message, and a reader may follow the empty one, find
nothing, and mark it read.

Which mode to use is the tradeoff in
[The remote reference is a commit permalink](#the-remote-reference-is-a-commit-permalink) below.
Same-day traffic between siblings is fine on local alone. Anything worth citing later wants the
push.

## Whoever writes a record commits it

Whoever writes a record is the one who commits it. In the same act is the ideal, since then no
moment holds an uncommitted record, but with today's handful of friendly participants a short
delay or batching a few writes into one commit is fine. What does not relax is the ownership:
nobody commits someone else's writing, which is what this repo has instead of a manager, because
ownership is per write rather than per repo.

## Concurrent writes collide, and the collision is normal

Every new record goes directly below its file's header, so two writers active at the same time
conflict at exactly the same lines. The merge is trivial, keep both records in either order, and
it is the expected cost of newest-first rather than an error. No record depends on its
neighbours, which is what makes the resolution safe.

## The remote reference is a commit permalink

The remote form is `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/<commit-sha>/<path>#<slug>`, and the
`<commit-sha>` is not optional.

- **A branch name rots.** A topic bookmark is deleted once its cycle lands, and the permanent
  branch does not carry the file until then, so both forms break at exactly the moment the
  message is worth reading.
- **A commit SHA does not.** It survives the bookmark's deletion, survives a rebase of anything
  after it, and resolves for a reader with no clone. GitHub's `y` key converts a branch URL into
  this form.
- **The local form names a path, the remote form names a version.** A local reference resolves to
  whatever that file says now, in whatever state that working copy happens to be, and it assumes

## Closed

The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). Earlier cycles are in the landmark commit's copy
of this section, and the cycles before the rule in the frozen [notes/chores/](notes/chores) and
[notes/done.md](notes/done.md).

### docs: adopt the family agent-files set

#### Problem

vc-x1 proposed one family set of agent-files, based on this repo's set as landed 2026-08-26 and
reworked as its cycle `docs: the family agent-files proposal` records (vc-x1 `main` a4309084fdfe,
the message in `vc-x1-messages/zc-ring-x1.md`). Our copy has drifted below it: it still carries
`cycle-checklists.md` and `cycle-protocol.md`, which nothing links anymore, cites `hard rule N` by
numbers that no longer exist, keeps the inline whys the set moved to rationale.md, and numbers its
`## Todo` entries. Beside that, `.vc-config.md` names this repo's family member as `vc-x1`, a copy
fossil, so the messaging acquaint check reads the wrong mailbox.

#### Solution

The set is adopted whole: `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*` are byte-identical to
vc-x1's at `a4309084fdfe`, `cycle-checklists.md` and `cycle-protocol.md` gone and
`commit-model.md` arrived. `TODO.md` has the set's seven sections with the Todo entries as
headings, the six live links that still pointed at moved `AGENTS.md` anchors are repointed into
the agent-data files, `.vc-config.md` names the member `zc-ring-x1`, and the dependencies moved to
their latest compatible versions on the way. The reply to vc-x1's record follows the landing, in
the durable mode, with the three remarks from the review (the Size close-out step, Restart as a
user step, Bullet form's reach over existing prose).

#### Acceptance check

`diff -r` of `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/` against vc-x1's at `a4309084fdfe` is empty, and
`custom.md` differs only in project content. `vc-x1 validate` passes, every agent-file link
resolves, and `grep -rn "hard rule [0-9]" AGENTS.md agent-data` finds nothing. The messaging
acquaint check opens `../vc-x1-messages/zc-ring-x1.md`.

Result: pass. `diff -r` against the set at `a4309084fdfe` is empty for `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`,
and `agent-data/` (custom.md identical too, since this project has no overrides). `vc-x1 validate`
passes, the link check finds nothing unresolved in the agent-files beyond their specimens, the
`hard rule` grep is empty, and `[family]` resolves to `../vc-x1-messages/zc-ring-x1.md`.

#### Ladder

- [docs: adopt the family agent-files set opening][1]
- [fix(config): name this repo's family member][4]
- [build: upgrade the dependencies to the latest compatible versions][6]
- [docs: copy the set over the agent-files][2]
- [docs: repoint the stale links into the agent-files][7]
- [docs: reshape TODO.md to the set's Todo format][3]
- [docs: adopt the family agent-files set closing][5]

#### Deliberation

- Accept the set whole, counter nothing in the copy: the rung copies vc-x1's files verbatim, so the
  three-way comparison the proposal names as its acceptance check goes empty for this member.
  - The three reservations from the review (the Size close-out step, Restart as a user step, and
    Bullet form's reach over existing prose) go in the reply as remarks, not as local edits, since a
    local edit would reopen the diff the proposal exists to close.
- The config fix is its own rung, first, not folded into the copy: it is not an agent-file, so
  `git log -- AGENTS.md agent-data/` keeps showing only rule changes, and it is the one line that
  breaks the messaging acquaint check today, so it lands before the set that runs the check.
- The dependency upgrade is a rung, not an entry: it arrived mid-opening, is small, and
  `vc-x1 validate` after it is its whole check, the rung-or-entry pick under the set's Unplanned
  work.
- The request became this block directly rather than a `## Todo` entry first: the opening is the
  same edit as moving an entry, and the record vc-x1's outcome will cite is this cycle's landmark.

#### Ladder details

##### docs: adopt the family agent-files set opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, write this
block, bump the version-of-record, and rename the artifact to `-dev`.

##### fix(config): name this repo's family member

`.vc-config.md` named the family member `vc-x1`, carried over when the file was copied from that
repo, so the messaging acquaint check would have opened vc-x1's record file rather than ours.

* The `[family] member` key is the only place the member name is stated, and it was the copy's.
  - It now reads `zc-ring-x1`, so `<family.messages>/<family.member>.md` resolves to
    `../vc-x1-messages/zc-ring-x1.md`, the file vc-x1's proposal was written to.

##### build: upgrade the dependencies to the latest compatible versions

The manifests asked for `clap 4.6.1` and the lock held transitive entries behind what their reqs
allowed, so a fresh build used older code than the reqs permitted.

* The manifest reqs were behind the latest compatible releases.
  - `cargo upgrade` moved `clap` to `4.6.6` in `tp_runner` and `tp_matrix`, the only req with a
    newer compatible version. No other req had one, and nothing was held behind an incompatible
    (major) release.
* The lock's transitive entries were behind their reqs.
  - `cargo update` moved eleven entries, `zerocopy` `0.8.52` to `0.8.56` and `hdrhistogram`
    `7.5.4` to `7.6.0` among them, with `nom` `7` to `8` and `zlib-rs` arriving as `hdrhistogram`'s
    new transitive choices and `minimal-lexical` leaving with the old `nom`.

##### docs: copy the set over the agent-files

Our agent-files were the base the set was built from, and the set's diff against them is the
proposal. Taking the set whole is what makes the three-way comparison empty for this member.

* `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/*` differed from the set in the ways the proposal lists.
  - Replaced by vc-x1's files at `a4309084fdfe`, taken from that commit rather than vc-x1's working
    tree, which had moved on. `commit-model.md` arrives, `cycle-checklists.md` and
    `cycle-protocol.md` go, and `agent-data/` and `AGENTS.md` are now byte-identical to the set.
* `custom.md` pointed at the old `## custom.md: the project layer` heading.
  - The anchor is `#custommd` now, and `custom.md` is identical to the set's too.
* `notes/README.md` linked the two retired files.
  - It names `jj.md`, `versioning.md`, and `cycle-model.md` instead. The other stale inbound
    anchors a link check found predate this rung and get the next one.

##### docs: repoint the stale links into the agent-files

Six links in live files still pointed at `AGENTS.md` anchors that moved into the agent-data files
before this cycle, when the prose, todo, and jj sections left AGENTS.md, so each resolved to the
top of the file rather than its section.

* `Prose form` was cited as `AGENTS.md#prose-form` in `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `notes/bugs.md`,
  `notes/todo-backlog.md`, and `notes/ring-buffer-design.md`.
  - Each now points at `agent-data/prose.md#prose-form`.
* `notes/todo-backlog.md` cited `AGENTS.md#todo-format` and `notes/jj-tips.md` cited
  `AGENTS.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers`.
  - They point at `agent-data/notes.md#todo-format` and
    `agent-data/jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers`.
* Three frozen files (`notes/chores/chores-01.md`, `chores-02.md`,
  `tprobe/notes/chores/chores-01.md`) carry the same stale anchors.
  - Left as they are: frozen history is never appended, and the link check's list is the record of
    where they point.

##### docs: reshape TODO.md to the set's Todo format

`TODO.md` had the numbered Todo shape the set retired, and lacked three of the set's sections, so
a citation of an entry had no anchor and the next agent had nowhere to leave continuation notes.

* The section list was `In Progress`, `Todo`, `Ideas`, with `## Closed` lost by this cycle's
  opening edit and no `## Bugs` pointer.
  - The set's seven sections are present in order, each with the intro vc-x1's carries:
    `## Continuation notes`, `## In Progress`, `## Closed`, `## Waiting`, `## Todo`, `## Ideas`,
    `## Bugs`. The three that hold nothing read `_None._`.
* The six `## Todo` entries were numbered list items, `N. Title: text`.
  - Each is a `###` heading titled by its lead phrase, its text the paragraph below, sub-bullets
    kept. Priority is file order, and the `fix-todo` instruction is gone from the intro. One
    untypeable character in an entry (`transfers are about 0`) converted with it.
* `## Ideas` entries stay bullets.
  - Unranked and never cited, so an anchor buys nothing there, and the intro now says how they are
    triaged, as vc-x1's does.
* `notes/todo-backlog.md`'s header described the rank-and-renumber scheme and `fix-todo`.
  - Rewritten to the set's wording, its dashes with it. It holds no entries. `notes/bugs.md` keeps
    its numbered entries and `fix-todo` note, since the set only asks that `## Bugs` point at it,
    and vc-x1's `bugs.md` is numbered too.

##### docs: adopt the family agent-files set closing

Closing out the cycle: run the acceptance check, finalize this block and move it to `## Closed`,
record the agent-files size, and bring the version-of-record to the bare `0.15.3`.

* The set's Close-out gained a Size step, which this repo had no file for.
  - `notes/agent-files-size.md` is created in vc-x1's shape with this cycle as its first row,
    2126 lines over 11 files, the same count as the set since the files are identical.
* Nothing in the block needs to outlive the cycle beyond what the size note now holds.
  - The link check that found the stale anchors was run by hand and is not kept, since the set's
    `validate` entry (vc-x1's `## Todo`) is the durable home for it.
* Close-out shape: trapezoid, the default. The ladder is five subjects, and `main` reads better as
  one commit per cycle with the rungs reachable behind it.
* `# Todo` over `## Todo`, and `# Bugs` over `## Bugs` in `notes/bugs.md`, slug to the same anchor,
  so a link to the section landed on the file's title (found by vc-x1, 2026-08-28).
  - The titles became `# Todo and cycle record` and `# Known bugs`, amended into this commit
    before the landing since the bookmark was still a draft.


## Waiting

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between

# 1. The message

**One body, two records.** The body goes in our repo at `messages/agent-files-adoption-0828.md` (our sender-side convention, `messages/`, which the protocol README's own specimen names), one `## Adoption and proposal 2026-08-28` section. Then two records, one in `../vc-x1-messages/vc-x1.md` and one in `../vc-x1-messages/zc-ring-x1.md`, both pointing at that section.

**Mode: fast/local.** Same-day sibling traffic, `local:` only, no push in between. The durable record comes later, when the adoption lands and there is a landmark permalink worth citing. That is the pattern zc-ring-x1 just used: local heads-up, durable reply after landing.

**Same pass, stamp `read:`** on vc-x1's 2026-08-28T15:56 record in our own file. It is unread today, and reading it is what tells them it arrived. Its `outcome-*` waits for the landing.

**What the body says**, four things:

1. We accept the set and will adopt it whole, taking **zc-ring-x1's copy at `6f91c4016812`** as the base, not vc-x1's at `a4309084fdfe`, because zc-ring-x1's differs by exactly one line and that line is its own accepted counter (markers stay in the closed block). Adopting vc-x1's would mean re-diverging on a point already settled.
2. One finding that should not wait for our cycle, because both of you are running with it today: **`agent-data/messaging.md` is linked from nothing.** Not `AGENTS.md`, not `custom.md`, not any other agent-data file, in either repo. With `## File map` gone, an agent following the set as written never learns the file exists, so its first rule, "At acquaint, check the record file", is unreachable. This session found vc-x1's proposal only because our `custom-family.md` says to look, and the adoption deletes that file.
3. A proposal cycle will follow, based on running the set rather than reading it, so it comes after we have used it for a cycle or two. Its likely content is in section 4 below.
4. Nothing in it is a condition of the acceptance.

I would **not** repeat zc-ring-x1's three remarks (Size step, Restart as a user step, Bullet form's reach). They are already on record with vc-x1 and re-sending them adds noise, not weight. Worth saying we read them and agree, in one sentence.

# 2. The adoption cycle

**Title** `docs: adopt the family agent-files set`, deliberately the same as zc-ring-x1's, so `git log --grep` reads the same across members. **Bookmark** `docs-adopt-the-family-agent-files-set`. **Versions** `0.26.2-0` at the opening through `0.26.2` at the closing, patch, and patch under either the old scope rule or the new default.

**Ladder, 8 rungs:**

1. `docs: adopt the family agent-files set opening` - create and publish the bookmark, write the In Progress block in the new shape, bump to `-0`, and carry the message body file.
2. `fix(config): convert the config to the markdown carrier` - `.vc-config.toml` to `.vc-config.md` on both sides, `repos.bot` to `repos.agent`, plus `[family]` (`iiac-perf` / `../vc-x1-template` / `../vc-x1-messages`) and `[validate]` (our four full commands and `cargo test --bins`). First, and separate, for zc-ring-x1's two reasons: it is not an agent-file, so `git log -- AGENTS.md agent-data/` keeps reading as rule changes only, and it is what makes the messaging acquaint check resolvable at all. Ours fails `vc-x1 config --validate` today, exit 1.
3. `docs: copy the set over the agent-files` - zc-ring-x1's `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, `agent-data/*` verbatim. `cycle-checklists.md` and `cycle-protocol.md` go (1163 lines), `commit-model.md`, `cycle-model.md`, `messaging.md`, `rationale.md` arrive.
4. `docs: empty custom-family.md into the set and config` - the file dissolves four ways: messaging into `agent-data/messaging.md` (already there, after checking nothing of ours is lost), medium and validation into the config from rung 2, member and template likewise, and the version promise into a `custom.md` override or nothing. The dogfood log needs a per-entry disposition, see below.
5. `docs: reshape TODO.md to the set's Todo format` - seven sections in order, the ten-plus numbered entries become `###` headings, priority by file order, `## Bugs` a pointer, `# References` at the foot.
6. `docs: repoint the stale links into the agent-files` - roughly twenty live references in `TODO.md`, `notes/README.md`, `notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/jj-tips.md`, `notes/bugs.md`, `docs/*`. Same rung freezes `notes/chores/` and `notes/done.md` with the header sentence zc-ring-x1 used, and leaves their stale anchors alone, since frozen history is never appended.
7. `fix(notes): the bugs file becomes an index` - the "index rather than a rank" wording, the `prose.md` link that currently points at a dead `../AGENTS.md#prose-form` anchor, and the em dash and multiplication sign in our one entry. Foldable into rung 6 if it looks thin.
8. `docs: adopt the family agent-files set closing` - acceptance check, finalize the block into `## Closed`, create `notes/agent-files-size.md`, full validation, `notes/README.md` if functionality changed, trapezoid, land.

**Acceptance check:** `diff -r` of `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/` against zc-ring-x1's at `6f91c4016812` is empty; `custom.md` differs only in project content; `custom-family.md` is gone; `vc-x1 config --validate` and `vc-x1 validate` both pass; `grep -rn "hard rule [0-9]"` over live files is empty; and the messaging acquaint check resolves `../vc-x1-messages/iiac-perf.md` from `[family]`.

# 3. Decisions I would want your call on

**The bootstrap.** This cycle starts under our current rules and ends under the new ones. The clean answer is that the record lives in `TODO.md > ## In Progress` from the **opening**, ahead of the rung that installs the set, because the closing has to move it to `## Closed` and it cannot do that from a chores file. So we adopt the record shape one rung before we adopt the files. zc-ring-x1 did the same. Worth stating in the deliberation rather than leaving to inference.

**Does `custom.md` keep a pointer?** zc-ring-x1's is the bare payload stub, `_None._`. Two options for us: bare stub, and the acceptance check goes empty on all three files, with the messaging hole left open until the family fixes the payload; or one pointer entry to `agent-data/messaging.md`, which the set explicitly blesses ("an agent-file asking for something in custom.md is answered by following the pointer") and which closes the hole locally today without reopening the diff. I lean to the pointer, and to saying so in the message, because the alternative is knowingly adopting a set whose mailbox check we cannot reach.

**Dev artifact name.** The set renames the artifact to `<name>-dev` at the opening "when the built artifact has consumers". We have none, by our own recorded promise. I would skip the rename and record that we skipped it and why.

**The dogfood log's nine entries.** It has no successor under the set, so each needs a disposition before rung 4 deletes it. Most are accepted per vc-x1's 2026-08-21 record and retire silently. The ones that were never answered need either a line in the message or a `## Waiting` entry. This is the one part of the adoption that is judgment rather than mechanics, and it is worth walking before the cycle opens, not during rung 4.

**Freezing is genuinely cheap, and worth confirming you agree.** All 130 chores references keep resolving. Nothing moves. The cost is only that two record systems sit side by side with a date as the boundary.

# 4. What I would propose, and when

Three items, and the timing matters more than the content.

1. **Make `messaging.md` reachable.** One line in `AGENTS.md`. I would argue for restoring a `## File map`, not a `## Working practices` bullet, because the same absence also hides `rationale.md`, `cycle-model.md` and `commit-model.md`, and because `rationale.md` still carries an orphaned `## File map` heading reading `_None recorded._` whose section no longer exists. Restoring the section fixes both. This one goes out **now**, with the heads-up, because both members are running with a broken acquaint check.
2. **`rationale.md`'s per-file sections are incomplete** - no `## messaging.md`, `## cycle-model.md`, `## commit-model.md`, against its own stated "one `##` per agent-file", and against its own rule that `_None recorded._` is a finding rather than a gap.
3. **Two corrections**, which their rule sends straight into the payload: `AGENTS.md` line 209 has an unbalanced paren ("distinct within its cycle [Commit description details][cdd])."), and `[cbt]` and `[cdd]` are two link labels resolving to one anchor.

Items 2 and 3 belong in a **separate convention cycle after the adoption**, per "convention work runs as its own cycle", and I would deliberately delay the substantive half of our proposal until we have run one or two real cycles under the set. Right now everything I have is from reading it. zc-ring-x1's three remarks are worth more than mine precisely because they came out of using it, and the honest thing is to earn ours the same way.

The plain version: send one local-mode heads-up to both siblings saying we accept, we are basing on zc-ring-x1 rather than vc-x1, and their messaging file is unreachable. Then run an eight-rung cycle that converts the config, copies zc-ring-x1's set, dissolves `custom-family.md`, reshapes `TODO.md`, and repoints the links, with the old chores frozen in place at no cost. Save the real proposal until we have used the set.

Four things I would like your call on before I touch anything: the `custom.md` pointer, skipping the dev rename, how to dispose of the dogfood log's nine entries, and whether the ladder is the right shape.

content.text:
Your feedback lands, and it inverts the main finding I brought you. Taking it in order.

## What changes

**My `messaging.md` fix was the wrong fix.** I proposed restoring a `## File map` so the orphaned file becomes reachable. Your answer is better: the file should not be in `agent-data/` at all. Move it to a family-shared custom layer and the unreachability dissolves as a side effect, because `custom.md` is the one file the rules already force an agent to read, and a pointer entry there is explicitly blessed. The bug I found is real, but it is a symptom of the file being in the wrong layer, not of a missing index.

**My rationale items go.** Proposal item 2 was "`rationale.md`'s per-file sections are incomplete, mirror the headings 1:1" - which is me asking for more of exactly the backlink machinery you are calling fragile. Withdrawn. The 1:1 mirrored-heading discipline is the fragile part: every heading rename breaks a pair silently, every rule owes a mirror, and eleven of them already read `_None recorded._`, which the file then defines as a finding rather than a gap. That is a maintenance obligation manufactured by the structure.

## The distinction, and whether I have it right

Let me state it back, because the plan hangs off it. The agent-files assume **two** repos that are coresident by construction - the work repo and the agent repo, guaranteed by the symlink. That assumption cannot fail. The family mechanism assumes **N sibling repos** coresident on one filesystem, which is a much stronger claim and fails the moment two members live on different machines or different people's laptops.

One refinement, because I think it sharpens rather than weakens your point. The messages repo is a git repo, so it travels; and the `remote:` field is a GitHub permalink, so durable-mode records resolve from anywhere. What is coresident-only is the `local:` field (`../vc-x1/notes/messages/...`), the config's relative `messages = "../vc-x1-messages"`, and the whole "resolve it from your sibling clone" reading model. So the mechanism is half portable and half not, and the half that is not is the half that makes it convenient. That is a worse position than either extreme, and it is an argument for your conclusion rather than against it.

The other half of your point I read as: hand-maintained field lists in markdown, with newest-first ordering, concurrent-write collisions declared "normal", and read receipts added by hand, is a database wearing a markdown costume. Agreed, and the same is true of rationale's anchor pairs. If those are placeholders, the adoption should do the **minimum** on both rather than the tidy thing.

One thing worth separating, because `rationale.md` currently blurs it: it names our `custom-family.md` as the measured failure behind "a rule adopted ahead lives in the agent-file, never a holding section". That claim is true of **rules awaiting convergence** hiding in the project layer. It is not true of **family-scoped content** living in a family-scoped file, which is a different thing that happened to share a file. Your position only contradicts the second, broader reading.

## What survives in the plan

Rungs 1, 2, 5, 6, 7 (config carrier, `TODO.md` reshape, link repoint, bugs file) are unaffected. Rung 3 (copy the set) and rung 4 (dissolve `custom-family.md`) both change, and `custom-family.md` no longer fully dissolves - it keeps its messaging half, or is replaced by whatever the family layer becomes. And the cycle stops being a clean acceptance: our diff is now non-empty by intent, so the proposal's own acceptance check, the three-way comparison going empty, is one we will not meet.

## Questions

**1. Where does the family layer physically live?** Four shapes, and they differ a lot in cost:

- Each member carries `custom-family.md` and they converge by diff, like the payload does. That is what we have today, and it is N copies to keep in sync.
- One file in the template repo, `../vc-x1-template/family.md`, each member's `custom.md` pointing at it. One copy, but a member without the template clone reads nothing.
- One file in the messages repo, beside the `README.md` that already governs the protocol. The content is about that repo, and every member that participates already has it cloned.
- No new file: fold the session-behavior half into the messages repo's own `README.md`, which is already the authority on record shape and modes, and have each member's `custom.md` point at it. `agent-data/messaging.md` is only 46 lines and most of it defers to that README already.

I lean to the last one. It is the only option with no copies and no new file, and it puts the rules in the repo they are about. But it makes a member's instructions depend on a repo it does not own, which may be exactly the coupling you want to avoid.

**2. How far do we go on rationale?** Adopt the file and quietly not honor the mirroring? Adopt it and counter the two rules that create the coupling (mandatory mirrored headings, and "the other agent-files carry no inline why, only the link")? Or not adopt it, and let short whys stay inline where they are, which is closer to what we carry now? The middle one is the real proposal, and it is a large one: 430 lines and most of the `[why]` links in `AGENTS.md`. I would want your read before drafting it, because "one way street, simple storage, no backlinks" could mean any of the three.

**3. Do we counter before adopting, or adopt then counter?** zc-ring-x1 has already landed the set. If we counter first and the family agrees, they re-sync once. If we adopt first and counter after, they re-sync twice and we copy in two files only to move them back out. Countering first is cleaner but costs a round trip and leaves us on the old set meanwhile. I lean to countering first on messaging, since it is a layer question that a copy would only obscure, and adopting everything else now.

**4. Does `[family]` stay in the config?** Our own `custom-family.md` argues that member name and template path "are environment rather than instruction" and belong in the config. That argument still holds under your position, and it splits cleanly: the machine-local paths stay in `.vc-config.md` where relative sibling paths are honest, and only the instruction half moves to the family layer. Confirming, because if the whole family concept is provisional you may want it out of the config too.

**5. Given both are placeholders for databases, should the adoption deliberately underinvest?** Concretely: do not create `notes/agent-files-size.md`, do not tidy rationale, keep the messaging text to the shortest thing that makes the acquaint check work, and spend no rung on either. I think yes, and it would shorten the ladder, but it means landing a set we already know we will churn.

iiac-perf 0.26.1 — Rust latency microbenchmark harness

Usage: iiac-perf [OPTIONS] [BENCHES]...

Arguments:
  [BENCHES]...
          Benches to run, or a command word ('all', 'qualify-environment',
          'describe-record', 'read-freq', 'pin-freq', 'restore-freq',
          'suggest-freq', 'add-completion-yaml').
          
          Pass 'all' for every registered bench, or one or more names; a name
          matching no bench exactly runs every bench it is a prefix of (e.g.
          'ice', 'mpsc'). Pass 'qualify-environment' (alone) to ask whether this
          machine is fit to measure on. Pass 'describe-record' (alone) to print
          the --record field dictionary. Pass 'read-freq', 'pin-freq [MHZ]', or
          'restore-freq' (alone) to read, pin, or restore the CPU clock. Pass
          'suggest-freq BENCH' to measure the best pin frequency under that
          bench's load. Pass 'add-completion-yaml' (alone) to write the carapace
          completion spec to the specs dir (see --completion-dir). Run with no
          args to see the available list.

Options:
  -d, --duration <DURATION>
          Target wall-clock seconds per bench.
          
          Default 5.0, or the config `duration`; auto-sizes outer and inner loop
          counts. Mutually exclusive with -D.

  -D, --total-duration <TOTAL_DURATION>
          Target total wall-clock seconds across all benches.
          
          The budget is split equally per bench. Mutually exclusive with -d.

  -o, --outer <OUTER>
          Override outer loop count (skips auto-sizing; inner still adapts)

  -i, --inner <INNER>
          Override inner loop count (skips auto-sizing).
          
          inner=1 measures single-call latency (each sample = one step); higher
          inner measures back-to-back/burst rate (each sample = N steps
          averaged).

      --pin-cpus <CPUS>
          Pin bench threads to CPUs (comma-separated, ranges OK).
          
          A CPU is the kernel's schedulable unit (sysfs cpuN, one affinity-mask
          bit); a physical core hosts two of them when SMT is on. The list is a
          CPU *pool*: thread `i` of a bench is pinned to `pool[i % pool.len()]`,
          so shorter pools oversubscribe by wrap. Examples: `--pin-cpus 0,1` (2
          threads → 2 CPUs), `--pin-cpus 0-5` (6-thread pool), `--pin-cpus 0,0`
          (two threads on the same CPU). On 3900X, CPUs N and N+12 are SMT
          siblings of the same physical core — `--pin-cpus 0,12` pairs siblings
          (max contention), `--pin-cpus 0,1` gives independent cores. A value
          naming a `[profiles]` entry in the config file expands to that
          profile's CPU spec (e.g. `--pin-cpus smt`). Omit to leave threads
          unpinned. `--pin` is a hidden alias.

  -v, --verbose
          Enable verbose internals on stderr (like `RUST_LOG=debug`).

content.text:
Ran both. Thoughts only, nothing changed.

## The tooling, and one honest limitation

`vc-x1-dev 0.80.6-8` has `validate-config` and `validate-anchors`. Run against us right now:

`validate-config` fails on the one thing we knew: `repos.bot` should be `repos.agent`, both sides.

`validate-anchors` fails with 8 problems across 27 files, and two of them are exactly the bug vc-x1 found and zc-ring-x1 fixed today:

- `TODO.md:49` - `## Todo` and the file's `# Todo` title slug to the same `#todo`, so every link to the section lands on the title. zc-ring-x1's fix was retitling to `# Todo and cycle record`.
- `notes/bugs.md:11` - same collision on `#bugs`. Their fix: `# Known bugs`.
- `docs/report-guide.md:219` - a genuinely broken link, `#comparing-two-implementations---blocks` against a heading that slugs to `#comparing-two-implementations-----------`. Ours, not inherited.
- `docs/report-guide.md:247`, `notes/jj-tips.md:326` - two more duplicate anchors.
- Two in `cycle-protocol.md`, which the adoption deletes.
- One unused reference definition in `README.md`.

So the tool pays for itself on our repo before we adopt anything, and it settles most of my "fragile links" objection. I agree with using tooling over rules here.

**The limitation worth knowing before you lean on it:** the run reports `173 cross-file skipped`. `validate-anchors` checks a markdown file's **own** anchors and references, not links into other files. Every case I was worried about is cross-file: `rationale.md`'s 1:1 mirrored headings, our stale `../AGENTS.md#prose-form` links, the `[why]` links from `agent-data/*` into `rationale.md`. None of those are covered today. That is a reason to want cross-file checking in the tool, not a reason to re-open the rules argument, and I am dropping the rules argument either way. I just do not want you deciding on the strength of a check that is narrower than it looks.

Your call on messaging lands it in `vc-x1-messages/README.md`, which is the no-copies option and puts the rules in the repo they are about. With "adopt and get to real work" as the frame, the ladder collapses to six rungs:

1. **opening** - bookmark, In Progress block in the new shape, version `0.26.2-0`.

**2. Which unbounded SPSC?** zc-ring-x1's forthcoming one, so the bench lands empty and fills in when they ship, or a third-party reference implementation to stand as a baseline now?

**3. Tokio: `block_on` per call, or inside a current-thread runtime?** My vote is inside the runtime, and to say plainly in the report that it is a different measurement from the sync channels rather than pretending the numbers are peers.

**4. Does the `[validate]` table get the two new validators?** They exist in `vc-x1-dev 0.80.6-8` but not in released `0.80.5`. Unless you would rather we run the dev build as a matter of course.

**5. Adopt minus `messaging.md`, or adopt whole and move it after?** Dropping it makes our diff against zc-ring-x1 one deleted file, which is a clean, legible proposal and matches your call. Adopting whole and moving it later is lower friction with the family but leaves us carrying a file we have decided does not belong. I lean to dropping it, and to editing the messages README in the same pass so nothing is homeless in between.

content.content:
## The cycle at a glance

Every change runs as a **cycle** with three phases: Preparation -> Work -> Close-out. The
phases always happen, but there are two styles. A **multi-step** cycle commits them
individually, as a ladder of steps (the Preparation commit is optional). A
**single-step** cycle folds all three into one commit when the change is straightforward, so
that one commit is the close-out and carries its duties. So a
single-step cycle is one commit, and a multi-step is minimum two (a Work commit plus the
close-out), typically three or more (the definition is
[AGENTS.md's Terminology](../AGENTS.md#terminology)). The
ladder lists a cycle's steps in order and identifies each by its title, with no number and no
version. Where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
[versioning.md](versioning.md). Read [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md) before any commit
work, and before any push, cycle or not.

## Cycles run on a bookmark

A cycle runs on one topic bookmark in the work repo, created at the opening and named by the
cycle title's slug (the anchor algorithm in
[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). `main` advances only when the
finished cycle lands on it, and nothing pushes straight to `main`. The bot repo needs no bookmark:
its `main` rides the tip of its linear narrative.

- **The bookmark is the unit of review.** Everything the cycle does is visible as one line
  against `main`, and until it lands the whole line is a draft that can be reshaped
  ([Topic bookmarks are drafts](#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts)). Landing is the single approval
  that makes the cycle permanent.
- **Create at the opening**, land at the close-out. Commands are in
  [Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land), and the opening's other duties are in
  the [Opening checklist](#opening-checklist) below.
- **A single-step cycle still gets one.** The saving is not worth the exception, and a
  one-commit line is exactly the case where a pre-landing rewrite is cheapest.
- **The permanent branch is whatever this project calls it** (`main` here). A long-lived program
  bookmark is a different animal, governed by
  [Long-lived bookmarks](jj.md#long-lived-bookmarks-merge-only-by-default-deletable-once-merged).

**Why:** a cycle that pushes `main` directly makes every correction a coordinated force-push of
published history. Landing costs one command and buys free rewrites for the whole cycle.

## Opening checklist

At the cycle's opening, before the first Work commit:

1. Create the cycle's bookmark ([Cycle bookmarks](jj.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
2. Move the picked-up item into `TODO.md > ## In Progress` and write the **six provisional
   items** there, all six required. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress`'s
   own level, and the other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###`
   title, `####` items, and under a program heading, each one deeper):
   - **title**, which becomes the chores section header at close-out
   - **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
   - **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad
   - **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?"
   - **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [[N]] [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with
     `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's `# References`. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`,
     is linked like the rest
   - **deliberation**: how the five above were decided (`_None._` when there was nothing to
     deliberate)
   A `Ladder details` area follows the six: one subsection per rung, closing included, headed
   by the rung's exact title, opened at laddering with the rung's intent and completed as rungs
   land, the closing rung's at close-out (see the protocol's
   [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation)).
3. Sweep `## Done` per [Retiring Done entries](notes.md#retiring-done-entries), then bump the
   version-of-record.

Nothing is opened in the chores file here. The block is the cycle's only home until close-out
moves it. See [Chores sections](cycle-protocol.md#chores-sections).

**Why the acceptance check:** a cycle's own checklists are per-commit instruments and every one
of them can pass while the banner claim is false. Measured in a seven-cycle program opened
against "end subprocess spawning": its close-out claimed the goal met, with about twenty spawn
sites surviving, two inside the facade the program built. A measurement or performance claim is
the shape most exposed, since "we measured it" is easy to believe and hard to notice you have not
done. Being provisional, the check can also be revised *toward* what was achieved, which is the
same failure by a slower route. A changed check is one of the things the deliberation justifies.

## Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`. Never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)). A
pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate. In
an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](cycle-protocol.md#policy).

## Topic bookmarks are drafts

A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch. Pushed there is not published.
So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**:
  - the bookmark has already landed
  - another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase
  - the ladder is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees

The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
[Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

## Per-commit checklist

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's

header, the Done entry, and the bookmark all derive from one bare title):

  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.

  not ready to be seen.

- `jj bookmark set main -r <bookmark> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.

## Retiring Done entries

`TODO.md`'s `## Done` section is a rolling buffer of recently shipped work, not a permanent
log. Move entries into `done.md` at these natural beats:

- **Closing a ladder**: when the close-out commit ships, decide which prior entries are no
  longer needed for nearby context and migrate them. The entry form is the same in both files
  (see [Done entry form](#done-entry-form)), so a migration moves the bullet as it stands.
- **Opening a new ladder**: at the opening step, do the same sweep before bumping the
  version-of-record.
- **Resolving an agent-file experiment**: at the beat where it resolves, not at a ladder
  boundary. Adopted and rejected retire identically, since "we tried this and dropped it" is what
  history serves worst. The narrative goes in a `chores-NN.md` section and the dogfood entry is
  removed from wherever the project keeps its log, so that log carries in-flight entries only. See
  [Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files).

Migration mechanics:

- Move the bullet itself from `TODO.md > ## Done` to `done.md` (preserving the original ref
  number).
- Copy any references the moved entries cite into `done.md`'s `# References` section (those
  refs are file-local, so coexisting with `TODO.md`'s namespace is fine).
- Prune any references in `TODO.md > # References` no longer cited by anything in
  `## In Progress` / `## Todo` / `## Done`. This frees the numbers for future reuse.

## Chores conventions

content.content:
### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / chores / commit)

A ladder step, its chores section, and its commit description share a *title* shape, a
[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`,
an optional `(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail.
They differ in the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the
[Commit-body form](#commit-body-form), ladder / chores are conceptual (see "Bullet *content*
differs by surface" above). The shared template:

```
<title>                          # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...
```

The three surfaces apply it as:

- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the rung is
  `- [[N]] [<title>][M] (marker)`: the as-built `[[N]]` placeholder carried from birth, the
  title reference-linked to the rung's subsection via `[M]: #<slug>` in the file's
  `# References` (the closing rung linked like the rest), and the `(current)` / `(done)` marker.
  Its position in the list is its position in the ladder. The last rung is the close-out and its
  text says so. Detail lives not on the rung but in the block's `Ladder details` subsection
  headed by the rung's exact title (see the protocol's
  [Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation)), bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
- **Chores section** (`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`): no prefix, since the `##` header *is* the
  bare title. The as-built ladder is the first content under it (see
  [Chores commit references](notes.md#chores-commit-references)).
- **Commit description**: no prefix. The title is the first line, and the body is the prose
  (see [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description)).

The title is **identical** across all three for a given step, so a step's ladder entry, its
chores `##` header, and its commit title line up verbatim. A `Ladder details` subsection
heading carries the same title, a fourth surface on every rung (the closing rung's exists only
when close-out gotchas occurred: see the protocol's
[Preparation](cycle-protocol.md#preparation)). Pick the commit title first and reuse it.

That identity is **per step**, not per cycle: each step in a cycle gets its own distinct
descriptive title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The cycle's chores
section header carries the *cycle title*, the bare name no multi-step commit carries (see the
bookends below). To keep a cycle's commits collectable with one `git log --grep`, give the
step titles a common greppable stem (e.g. `config loader`).

**Cycle bookend titles**: a multi-step cycle's bookend commits are the cycle title plus a
suffix, " opening" and " closing", same type (`feat: dynamic warmup opening` /
`feat: dynamic warmup closing`), so one `git log --grep "<cycle title>"` returns the pair that
brackets the ladder. The bare cycle title is the cycle's *name*: the chores `##` header and
the `## Done` entry carry it, and no multi-step commit does, which is also what keeps the
closing rung's subsection anchor clear of the section header's. A single-step cycle's one
commit is the cycle and keeps the bare title. The type repeats across the pair even though the
bookends are mostly bookkeeping: identical prefixes make them scannable. Rungs between keep
their own titles on the stem.

### Steps are named, not numbered

A step has a title and no number. Nothing in a ladder rung, a chores as-built rung, a `## Done`
entry, or a commit gives a step an ordinal: a rung's place in the list already *is* its place in
the ladder, so a number beside it would restate the position and then have to be maintained.

- **The title is the identifier.** A record points at a step by its title, a plain greppable
  mention, which is why the title is verbatim-identical across the three surfaces.
- **Unambiguous, not globally unique.** Two titles must be distinguishable in the two places a
  title is resolved: within its own cycle, so a ladder rung names one step, and within its chores
  file, since a `##` header is also an anchor and a repeated slug silently dedupes to the first
  one. Across the repo's history a title may repeat.
- **Nothing renumbers.** Inserting, reordering or dropping a step edits the ladder list and
  nothing else. On an unlanded topic bookmark the rungs that already committed an older ladder
  come along. See
  [Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).
- **`## Todo` ranks are the exception that stays numbered**, because a priority list has an order
  worth reading off (see [Todo format](notes.md#todo-format)). Those numbers are positional too,
  and are equally never used as references.

### Versions live in the version-of-record only

No version appears in durable prose: not in an in-flight ladder rung, a chores header, a commit
title, or a commit body. The manifest is the version's only written home (see
[versioning.md](versioning.md)), and a commit's version is read from that file at that
commit.

**Why:** the version is a build stamp answering "which commit produced this artifact", not a name
for a step. Written into prose it becomes a second identifier that history is free to invalidate:
one renumber of published versions turns every prose mention, transcript and pasted report into
residue that needs a decoder to read. A renumber cannot touch a title.

**Two surfaces record a version rather than name a step.** Both record a *commit*, never a step,
which is what keeps them outside the rule rather than exceptions to it:

- **A chores as-built rung** records a version alongside that commit's SHA once the commit is on
  a permanent branch. The pair decodes an old `-V` banner or a pasted report. It obeys the SHA's
  timing exactly, so a rung on an unlanded branch carries neither (see
  [Chores commit references](notes.md#chores-commit-references)).
- **A `## Done` entry**, in `TODO.md` and in `done.md`, carries the close-out's version ahead of
  its title (see [Done entry form](notes.md#done-entry-form)). Here the version is the search
  key: the question a reader arrives with is "what shipped in 0.42.0", and with no version
  written anywhere in the Done list that question has no answer.

The two differ in timing, and the reason is the SHA rather than the version. The rung waits
because a commit cannot record its own SHA. A Done entry has no SHA to wait for and its version
is already in the manifest of the commit it is written in, so it is written at close-out. On an
unlanded bookmark it is a draft like the rest of the line
([Topic bookmarks are drafts](cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts)), and a renumber of
published versions rewrites it in the same sweep as the rungs.

**How to apply:** name the step by its title and the phase in words ("the close-out", "the
opening"). Writing *about* versioning is unaffected: a version named as a specimen, whether in the
scheme's own notation, a decoder table, or a narrative about a renumber, is a use of the word
rather than an identifier for a step, the same distinction
[Typeable punctuation only](#typeable-punctuation-only) draws between naming a character and using
one. Existing versioned prose is grandfathered and converts when touched, no sweep.
